scope: Actual native OTIO viewer, not the clickable mock. Read all eight refreshed path PNGs and eight 320px supplemental PNGs from the pushed capture revision. Read its 30-row native-controls-measurements.json as a separate DOM receipt. No product build, test, formatter, or vendor write was run during this review.

methods.pngByEye: Read each original native PNG and zoomed critical controls. Screenshot observations cannot establish DOM hit testing or hidden overflow.
methods.pngPixels: Counted representative opaque RGB foreground and background pixels inside rendered Post, Preview base, Comment, and Play buttons, excluding antialiased edges. Ratios use WCAG relative luminance. Cropped view magnification does not change the original pixel measurements.
methods.domReceipt: The separate browser measurement JSON supplies geometry, page/timeline overflow, sidebar states, and hovered Post computed colors. It is browser evidence produced with these native screenshots by the parent integration run, not inferred from PNGs.

geometryFromNativeDom.closedTab: At 1440, 390, and 320px in both schemes, the DOM receipt places the closed tab outside the stage before and after stage/timeline scrolling. All enumerated transport, inspector, timeline, selection and select control boxes are within the stage and not tab-covered. All six exposed selects retain their arrow area. Zoomed 1440 PNG shows the select ending about x1398 and tab starting about x1411, a visible 13px gap.
geometryFromNativeDom.sidebar: In both desktop schemes, the open thread starts immediately after the stage with 0px gap, resizer visible and edge tab hidden; closing restores the tab. In both 390 and 320 schemes the open thread owns the row, resizer is hidden, gap is 0px, and closing restores the stage/tab.
geometryFromNativeDom.composerComponents: All six composer-normal and six composer-hover measurements report context, textarea, Post, Cancel and disclosure visible and within the stage. Screenshot inspection independently confirms no foreground text or control is clipped.

contrastFromActualNativePixels.control: Preview base media without unsupported effects

postHoverFromNativeDom.note: Hover was measured in the native DOM receipt, not captured in the static PNGs.

resolvedComparedWith97593f9: Previously, the desktop Comments edge tab covered approximately 29px of the select and hid its arrow in all four 1440 captures. Final captures show a visible gap and unobstructed arrow.

Previously, white dark-mode composer Post ink on #4fb3a6 measured 2.521:1. Final actual dark ink measures 6.885:1 in 390 and 320 PNGs and in normal/hover DOM receipts. The captured Post selector is .popover-card .popover-action.is-primary, not .action.primary.

currentDefects.evidence: At 320px the Incomplete preview scope text and first lines of the blocked-preview status are superimposed near the top of the dark stage, approximately x16..270, y70..110. Zoomed PNG pixels show both strings occupying the same rows, making the status opening unreadable. The teal Preview base button below is separately legible. This is a screenshot observation; the existing DOM receipt did not measure text ink overlap.
currentDefects.status: Open visual defect, reported to integration owner before any additional UI edits.

limits: The eight primary captures show the ordinary preview and composer; the separate 320px supplemental captures are required to inspect Preview base and Comment selection. Neither control was present in the older eight-image-only review.

PNG pixels establish appearance but not clickability. Native DOM receipt establishes control rectangles and page overflow, not text-ink collision, which the separate blocked-preview screenshot exposes.
This audit certifies neither the full source PATH nor external publish/deploy state. It records visual evidence only.
designRead: The restrained square editor chrome and patina controls remain tied to the existing Relic visual system. Reject shrinking type or an unrelated new design to hide layout defects; the new scope/status overlap requires a targeted readability correction.
